rows.title: Boeing To Pay $2.5 Billion Over 737 Max Fraud, Faces No Other Charges
rows.standfirst: "Boeing's employees chose the path of profit over candor," Justice Department officials said, after reaching a deal with Boeing. Most of the funds will pay airlines whose planes were grounded.

rows.title: Rhode Island Gov. Gina Raimondo Is Biden's Commerce Secretary Pick
rows.standfirst: If confirmed, Gov. Gina Raimondo, the first woman to lead Rhode Island, would oversee the Census Bureau as it finishes a fraught national count that has been upended by COVID-19 and Trump officials.

rows.title: Why West Virginia's Winning The Race To Get COVID-19 Vaccine Into Arms
rows.standfirst: To get vaccines into long-term care facilities, West Virginia was the only state to opt out of a federal partnership with CVS and Walgreens. Instead, a network of smaller pharmacies got a jump-start.

rows.title: How Political Instability Affects The Economy
rows.standfirst: We're only seven days into the new year and we're off to a bumpy start. But as chaos rages through the capitol, the stock market and other signs of economic growth continue.

rows.title: Facebook Bans President Trump From Posting For The Rest Of His Presidency
rows.standfirst: The move is the most severe punishment any social media company has taken in response to Trump, who used online platforms to encourage the violent mob that stormed the Capitol on Wednesday.

rows.title: Twitter Locks Trump's Account, Warns Of 'Permanent Suspension' If Violations Continue
rows.standfirst: Twitter on Wednesday put President Trump on notice: If he does not stop breaking the platform's rules, he will be permanently banned.

rows.title: Fear And Loaning
rows.standfirst: There's a fear radiating out from the commercial real estate market — a fear that some economists say could become a drag on any economic recovery. In fact, there's evidence it already has.

rows.title: Major Oil Companies Take A Pass On Controversial Lease Sale In Arctic Refuge
rows.standfirst: After a three-year push by the Trump administration, almost no oil companies offered bids. Analysts point to controversy, low oil prices and an incoming administration that opposes drilling.

rows.title: Germany Moves Toward Requiring Women On Large Companies' Executive Boards
rows.standfirst: Germany lags the U.S. and others in the number of women on boards at major companies. "[N]ot many changes are made voluntarily, and progress is very slow," said the federal minister for women.

rows.title: NYSE Reverses Itself Again, Moving To Delist 3 Large Chinese Telecoms
rows.standfirst: The reversal comes one day after Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin reportedly criticized the New York Stock Exchange's decision not to delist the companies.

rows.title: New Year, New Indicators
rows.standfirst: 2020 was a tough year for the economy. How different will 2021 be? Today on the show, we take a look at three of our favorite indicators for the new year.

rows.title: Have You Been Evicted During The Pandemic, Or Afraid Of Losing Your Home?
rows.standfirst: NPR wants to hear from you if you have lost income and couldn't pay rent to your landlord or needed a mortgage forbearance.

rows.title: NYSE Will Not Delist 3 Chinese Telecoms Trump Administration Wanted Removed
rows.standfirst: The Trump administration has alleged that some Chinese companies funnel money to China's military. China had threatened to retaliate for the move.

rows.title: Hospitals Forced To Be More Transparent About Pricing. Will That Save You Money?
rows.standfirst: Under a rule that kicked in Jan. 1, hospitals must now make public the prices they negotiate with health insurers. But health policy experts have divergent views on what that will mean for patients.

rows.title: The Economy In 2030
rows.standfirst: What will the global economy look like in a decade? Mauro Guillen joins the show to talk about 2030, his new book where he analyzes the economic trends of the future.

rows.title: $1,400 Checks And Help For The Jobless: What's In Biden's Plan To Rescue The Economy
rows.standfirst: President-elect Joe Biden is proposing a $1.9 trillion plan to address the coronavirus pandemic and the resulting economic crisis.

rows.title: Making Sense Of Pandemic Stats
rows.standfirst: Statistics and the information we get from them have a massive influence on our worldviews and the decisions we make, but how can we ensure we're interpreting them properly? Today, we find out.

rows.title: U.S. Still Lags In COVID-19 Workplace Safety, Former OSHA Official Says
rows.standfirst: Ten months into the pandemic, the Trump administration is neglecting safety at meatpacking plants and other workplaces, a former top federal official says.

rows.title: 'Artists, Weirdos, Hellriders And Homies:' Thrasher Magazine Turns 40
rows.standfirst: Thrasher magazine was founded 40 years ago in San Francisco to cover skateboarding. Over the next four decades, the black-and-white newsprint magazine grew into a full color cultural arbiter.

rows.title: Jack Dorsey Says Trump's Twitter Ban Was 'Right Decision' But Worries About Precedent
rows.standfirst: Twitter kicked President Trump off its site following the insurrection at the U.S. Capitol. The CEO said major corporations have too much power and pose a risk to a "free" Internet.

rows.title: Nervous TikTok
rows.standfirst: The U.S. was going to ban TikTok... and then it didn't. We break down the beef with TikTok, and see what life would have been like without it. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: FAA Cracks Down On Unruly Airline Passengers Ahead Of Biden Inauguration
rows.standfirst: After incidents of Trump supporters engaging in threatening and disruptive behavior on flights to and from Washington, D.C., last week, the FAA enacts a "zero tolerance" policy.

rows.title: Companies Get Political
rows.standfirst: Politics used to be off limits for most American companies — at least publicly. Most would usually take a neutral position when a big political story hit the news. But that has changed.

rows.title: Amazon Says Parler Systematically Unwilling To Remove Violent Content
rows.standfirst: Parler sued after Amazon Web Services booted it off the public Internet. The cloud service says the site has allowed threatening and hateful posts, even after last week's riot at the Capitol.

rows.title: Airbnb Is Canceling All Reservations In Metro D.C. During Inauguration Week
rows.standfirst: The company also said it has banned "numerous individuals" that it found to be associated with hate groups or involved in criminal activity at the Capitol.

rows.title: New York City Cancels Contracts With Trump Organization
rows.standfirst: Mayor Bill de Blasio said that President Trump "incited a rebellion" and that New York City "will not be associated with those unforgivable acts in any shape, way or form."

rows.title: Should The Government Pay People To Get Vaccinated? Some Economists Think So
rows.standfirst: Dr. Anthony Fauci says the country will likely need a vaccination level of between 70% and 90% to reach herd immunity. Right now, that math doesn't quite add up.

rows.title: After Deadly Capitol Riot, Fox News Stays Silent On Stars' Incendiary Rhetoric
rows.standfirst: Many Fox News hosts, commentators and guests helped stoke the pro-Trump protests that became an assault on Congress. Among those influenced was Ashli Babbitt, who died while storming the Capitol.

rows.title: YouTube Joins Twitter, Facebook In Taking Down Trump's Account After Capitol Siege
rows.standfirst: The move, which suspends the president's account for a week, comes after the video platform said a livestream of his remarks on Tuesday violated YouTube's community standards.

rows.title: Auto Production Disrupted By Chip Shortages: A Dream Car May Be Hard To Find
rows.standfirst: Computer chips are an essential component for new cars. But car production has recovered faster than expected, and competing demand for semiconductors has also been rising. Some plants are struggling.

rows.title: Economics In Space
rows.standfirst: Economics is the earthiest of the social sciences. But its principles apply equally in space. The difference is how certain goods, services and even experiences gain currency in zero gravity.

rows.title: Trump Ally At Voice of America Replaced By News Executive He Recently Demoted
rows.standfirst: The Biden White House has named Yolanda Lopez acting director of the Voice of America. She was demoted last week after a VOA reporter asked Secretary of State Mike Pompeo unwelcome questions.

rows.title: Facebook Asks Oversight Board Whether Trump's Account Should Be Restored Now
rows.standfirst: The social network referred its decision to revoke the former president's posting privileges to its Oversight Board, an independent panel of experts.

rows.title: Judge Refuses To Reinstate Parler After Amazon Shut It Down
rows.standfirst: U.S. District Judge Barbara Rothstein sided with Amazon, which argued that Parler would not remove posts from its site that threatened public safety in the wake of the Capitol riot.

rows.title: Unemployment Claims Stay Stubbornly High As Biden Takes Office
rows.standfirst: New claims for state unemployment benefits dipped last week but remained high, showcasing the economic challenges facing President Biden.

rows.title: Trader Joe's, Dollar General And Others Are Paying Workers To Get Vaccines
rows.standfirst: Grocers from Aldi to Trader Joe's are pitching financial incentives to their employees to encourage them to get vaccinated.

rows.title: Pandemic Drastically Cut Emissions From Cars. The Lone Exception? SUVs
rows.standfirst: In rich countries, every sector of the economy reduced its contribution to climate change last year — with one big gas-guzzling exception.

rows.title: Stocks Close On Record Highs After Biden Inauguration
rows.standfirst: The Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq all hit new records as markets closed on Wednesday. Former President Donald Trump frequently cited stock market gains as a personal accomplishment.

rows.title: Biden's Econ Plan: 3 Indicators To Watch
rows.standfirst: President Biden recently announced his $1.9 trillion American Rescue Plan, targeting pandemic relief and economic recovery. We discuss 3 indicators to watch to measure the Biden economic agenda's success in the coming years.

rows.title: Defined By Scandal At Voice of America, CEO Resigns At Biden's Request
rows.standfirst: Michael Pack's record at the parent agency for the Voice of America includes charges of bias, firings, investigations and more. He called President Biden's request for him to resign a "partisan act."

rows.title: Biden To Extend Order Limiting Pandemic Evictions
rows.standfirst: On his first day in office, the president plans to sign an executive order extending the CDC's moratorium on evictions. Housing advocates say the CDC rule needs to be strengthened.

rows.title: President Biden Extends Student Loan Payment Freeze Through Sept. 30
rows.standfirst: Following an official action from President Biden Wednesday, the Education Department extended pandemic relief from payments for about 41 million federal student loan borrowers through Sept. 30.

rows.title: Biden Order Blocks Keystone XL Pipeline
rows.standfirst: This likely means the end of the $8 billion pipeline, a years-long project that would have carried oil sands crude from Alberta, Canada, to the American Gulf Coast.

rows.title: Modern Monetary Theory (Classic)
rows.standfirst: We rethink everything we know about government spending, taxes, and the nature of money.

rows.title: DOJ Drops Insider Trading Investigation Into Sen. Richard Burr
rows.standfirst: Officials launched a probe into Burr's business dealings after he warned some constituents in February to prepare for the coronavirus. Two weeks earlier he had sold off $1.7 million in stocks.

rows.title: Meeting With Republicans On COVID-19 Relief, White House Says Biden 'Will Not Settle'
rows.standfirst: After the meeting, the White House said the president "will not slow down work on this urgent crisis response, and will not settle for a package that fails to meet the moment."

rows.title: Reddit WallStreetBets Founder Calls GameStop Stock Frenzy A 'Symbolic Movement'
rows.standfirst: Jaime Rogozinski, a former moderator of the now-famous Reddit forum that sent GameStop stock soaring, saw the chaos coming. For too long, Wall Street has been "an invite-only club," he says.

rows.title: Vaccines For Data: Israel's Pfizer Deal Drives Quick Rollout — And Privacy Worries
rows.standfirst: Israel paid a premium, locked in an early supply of Pfizer-BioNTech vaccines and agreed to share data from Israel's centralized trove of medical statistics. Privacy advocates have some misgivings.

rows.title: Unwelcome On Facebook And Twitter, QAnon Followers Flock To Fringe Sites
rows.standfirst: As Twitter and Facebook crack down on those spreading baseless QAnon conspiracies, adherents are finding other apps to communicate on, including platforms where they may be further radicalized.

rows.title: WallStreetBets Founder Is 'Fascinated' Watching GameStop Frenzy From Sidelines
rows.standfirst: Reddit's WallStreetBets community was central to this week's stock market insanity. NPR's Michel Martin speaks with Jaime Rogozinski, the founder and former moderator of that group.

rows.title: Promising COVID-19 Vaccine News Has Some Itching To Travel Again
rows.standfirst: "People are tired of being at home," one travel advisor says as an industry decimated by the pandemic begins to see small signs that a recovery might be on the way.

rows.title: CDC Issues Sweeping New Mask Mandate For U.S. Travelers, Extends Eviction Moratorium
rows.standfirst: The new travel order will require passengers to wear face coverings on nearly all forms of public transportation, including airplanes, ships, ferries, trains, subways, buses, taxis and ride-shares.

rows.title: Can't Stop GameStop
rows.standfirst: Video game stores. Hedge Funds. Reddit forums. How this mad lib resulted in the biggest short squeeze in years. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: Should We Raise The Minimum Wage?
rows.standfirst: Biden is calling for a $15 federal minimum wage. Is that a good idea for workers and small businesses? Stacey and Cardiff duke it out.

rows.title: New York City Could Allow Indoor Dining For Valentine's Day
rows.standfirst: New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo will allow indoor dining at New York City restaurants on Feb. 14, if coronavirus cases continue along their downward trend. Restaurants would operate at 25% capacity.

rows.title: Itching To Travel Again, Some Americans Take Advantage Of Lower Airfare
rows.standfirst: Despite a slow vaccine rollout, Americans are hoping they'll be able to travel safely soon. And with relatively low airfares and flexible change policies, some are planning that next big trip.

rows.title: From Elon Musk To AOC, Everybody Has A Tweet About GameStop
rows.standfirst: Jon Stewart and Ted Cruz are among other high-profile people who took to Twitter to comment on the stock story gripping the country.

rows.title: Shell Ordered To Compensate Nigerian Farmers Affected By Oil Spills
rows.standfirst: "Finally, there is some justice for the Nigerian people suffering the consequences of Shell's oil," said Eric Dooh, one of the Nigerian farmers who sued Shell.

rows.title: Game Back On: GameStop Stock Rebounds As SEC Warns Against Market Manipulation
rows.standfirst: The video game retailer's shares shoot up, the online broker Robinhood struggles for cash and securities regulators issue a stern warning for anyone trying to game the market.

rows.title: For Amazon and Alabama, Warehouse Union Vote Would Shake Up History
rows.standfirst: If workers from Amazon's warehouse near Birmingham vote to unionize in the next two months, they would turn a new page not only for the company but for the region.
